messages.author: bb723ef8c9a6e579
messages.subject: STATE-SPACE MODELS rw1
parts:
Dear inla users,

We are trying to fit a state-space model, in particular:

y_t \sim N(x_t, tau_y)
x_t=x_{t-1} + epsilon_t
epsilon_t \sim N(mu_e, tau_e)

We can fit that in INLA using a rw1 where prior for epsilon_t is N(0, tau_e). However, we would like to give a prior for mu_e. Is there any possibility to do it?, or fixed it to another value different of zero?

Thank you,

Best regards,

Joaquín.

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] STATE-SPACE MODELS rw1
parts:
Is it possible to rewrite this as
x = f1 + f2
where f1 is a rw1 (with mu=0), 
and f2=mu*t
?

If this model is equivalent, you can add a copy of "t" as a covariate (with beta=mu), or fix it as an offset (mu*t).

PS. It will always be possible to do with rgeneric, I am just trying to find a simpler solution.

Kind regards,
Haakon

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] STATE-SPACE MODELS rw1
parts: Not entirely correct, the solution is much simpler:

N<-1000
i<-1:N
j<-i

datos<-data.frame(y, i , j)
formula<- y ~ -1 + f(i, model='rw1', fixed=TRUE) + j

Here, you have an almost flat prior for beta_j (=mu). Since this is a fixed effect, the posterior is usually not at all sensitive to the prior. You can set a different Gaussian prior by changing the fixed effect precision, see "?control.fixed".

## Suggestion to set a prior:
- To set prior, you could define an overall iid effect, weighted by j:

constant = rep(1, N)
f(constant, model="iid", weights=j, hyper = ...)

- I have not tested this, so not 100% certain.
- Can someone else confirm this?

Kind regards,
Haakon

or

f(idx, weight, model=..., hyper=...)
